skills.title: Controlled end-to-end feature QA
skills.summary: Turns a ticket and its implementation into a version-bound, evidence-backed QA run with explicit approvals, deterministic release rules, regression protection, publication, and cleanup.
skills.use_when: Use for meaningful product changes that require code-aware impact analysis, planned execution, traceable evidence, defect triage, and a release recommendation.
skills.not_for: Do not use for one-line copy edits, emergency production operations, or any environment where deployment identity and test-data ownership cannot be verified.

phases.name: Secure preflight and deployment attestation
phases.desc: Resolve the ticket, PR, repositories, environment, authenticated role, feature flags, browser context, and deployment manifest. Validate that the deployed artifact contains the approved source commits.
phases.detail: ticket version · PR head/base · source commit map · artifact digest · environment identity · role · browser · viewport

phases.name: Requirements and change-impact analysis
phases.desc: Read acceptance criteria, diff, related code, routes, types, permissions, existing tests, dependencies, migrations, and observability. Record contradictions as requirement gaps instead of inventing behaviour.
phases.detail: direct impact · indirect impact · security · accessibility · compatibility · migration · observability

phases.name: Risk-based test plan
phases.desc: Create numbered scenarios with priority, preconditions, steps, expected results, assertion type, evidence type, test matrix, stop conditions, required status, and explicit exclusions.
phases.detail: P0–P3 · positive · negative · edge · regression · roles · browsers · devices · account states

phases.name: Data, side-effect, and execution authorization
phases.desc: List every create, update, delete, feature-flag change, external notification, stub, mock, webhook, download, and cleanup action. Bind approval to the hashed data plan and run context.
phases.detail: idempotency keys · ownership IDs · test sinks · no hidden writes · reversible changes

phases.name: Execution and assertion-specific evidence
phases.desc: Run required scenarios in priority order. Record every attempt separately and capture evidence appropriate to the assertion rather than treating screenshots as universal proof.
phases.detail: screenshots · traces · video · network · logs · timing · persistence checks · first failure retained

phases.name: Finding classification and defect confirmation
phases.desc: Classify non-pass results as product defect, environment failure, automation failure, data failure, requirement gap, third-party failure, security concern, or unknown. Search for candidate duplicates without suppressing legitimate findings.
phases.detail: reproduction attempted · confidence recorded · candidate duplicates reviewed

phases.name: Regression protection
phases.desc: Recommend the lowest reliable test layer and validate generated tests through red-to-green proof or an approved alternative when the broken state cannot be safely recreated.
phases.detail: unit · component · contract · API · integration · Playwright · stable selectors · isolated data

phases.name: Decision, publication, and cleanup
phases.desc: Revalidate deployment and approvals, calculate the ordered release outcome, review evidence, publish one idempotent ticket update, render the report bundle, and clean only verified owned resources.
phases.detail: context revalidation · override recorded separately · cleanup residuals listed · resumable checkpoints

verdicts.label: PASS
verdicts.desc: All required steps ran and the approved expected result was directly observed with valid evidence.

verdicts.label: FAIL
verdicts.desc: The controlled scenario ran and the actual result contradicted the approved expectation.

verdicts.label: INCONCLUSIVE
verdicts.desc: Execution completed, but expectation or evidence remains genuinely ambiguous.

verdicts.label: BLOCKED
verdicts.desc: A verified prerequisite outside the scenario prevented completion.

verdicts.label: NOT TESTED
verdicts.desc: The scenario was not attempted and the reason is recorded.

verdicts.label: FLAKY
verdicts.desc: Controlled attempts produced inconsistent product outcomes. It is never converted to PASS.

evidence: Asserted element and relevant context are visible, readable, and timestamped.
Trace or video plus URL history
Origin, destination, intermediate state, and timing are preserved.
Method, endpoint, status, schema, and approved relevant headers match.
Role attestation plus UI and API evidence
Tenant, ownership, operation, and role are independently verified.
Approved API or read-only data verification
State survives reload or a new session without hidden caching.
Threshold, sample count, variance, browser, build, and environment are recorded.
Observation duration and interruptions are explicit.
New errors are separated from a versioned, expiring baseline.
controls: The runtime, not the prompt, enforces filesystem, command, repository, secret, and network permissions.
Every approval stores the approver, timestamp, role, document hash, context hash, expiry, and invalidation reason.
Deployment, role, tenant, feature flags, and relevant configuration are rechecked before execution, resume, decision, and publication.
Untrusted values are HTML-escaped, Markdown-safe, length-bounded, link-validated, and never used directly as paths.
Events are sequenced and hash-chained; evidence manifests include capture context and are signed when stronger assurance is required.
Sensitive headers are filtered before storage; raw and publishable evidence have separate access, retention, and redaction policies.
Run locks, idempotency keys, unique IDs, and compare-and-update operations prevent silent overwrites.
Real returned resource IDs are recorded immediately; cascade impact and cleanup uncertainty require explicit review.

decisions.label: INVALID RUN
decisions.desc: Deployment identity, approval binding, environment integrity, or evidence integrity cannot be established.

decisions.label: REJECT
decisions.desc: An unresolved release-blocking product, security, data-integrity, or compliance defect exists.

decisions.label: BLOCKED
decisions.desc: Any required scenario is blocked, inconclusive, not tested, flaky, or ended in an execution error.

decisions.label: CONDITIONAL PASS
decisions.desc: All required scenarios passed, but explicitly accepted optional gaps or residual risks remain.

decisions.label: PASS
decisions.desc: All required scenarios passed, no unaccepted release-blocking risk remains, and cleanup state is acceptable.

boundaries: A preview may use a synthetic merge commit or several repositories; validate a deployment manifest rather than comparing only one SHA.
Some defects cannot be reproduced safely. Reproduction is attempted, but strong original evidence may still justify a finding.
A short observation cannot establish long-term stability; duration and confidence remain visible.
Database, infrastructure, and security checks require explicitly approved read-only mechanisms or isolated environments.
Third-party availability and rate limits are classified separately from product behaviour.
Generated regression tests remain proposed changes until reviewed and validated in the target repository.
skills.example_request: Run /feature-qa for ticket QA-1234 against preview environment qa-preview-1234. Review the PR, test as both Admin and Member, and do not publish anything until I approve.
skills.example_output:
Outcome: BLOCKED

Reason:
Required Member permission scenario could not be completed because the preview API returned an environment-wide authentication error.

Verified:
- Deployment manifest contains the approved frontend and API commits.
- Admin happy path passed.
- No production origin was contacted.
- Test data remains isolated under run QA-1234-01.

Next action:
Restore preview authentication, revalidate the run context, and resume from scenario P0-03.

skills.title: Requirement and testability review
skills.summary: Reviews a Jira or Linear ticket before implementation or QA begins, exposing ambiguity, contradiction, hidden dependencies, missing acceptance criteria, and untestable expectations.
skills.use_when: Use during refinement, grooming, design review, or before a developer begins implementation.
skills.not_for: Do not use as a substitute for product decisions, legal approval, security threat modelling, or technical design ownership.

phases.name: Source and version preflight
phases.desc: Fetch the exact ticket revision, linked designs, API contracts, parent initiatives, dependent tickets, and referenced incidents. Record inaccessible sources instead of guessing.
phases.detail: ticket ID · revision · author · status · links · attachment hashes

phases.name: Intent extraction
phases.desc: Separate the customer problem, business outcome, proposed solution, acceptance criteria, constraints, assumptions, and explicit exclusions.
phases.detail: problem · actor · desired outcome · proposed behaviour · non-goals

phases.name: Ambiguity and contradiction analysis
phases.desc: Detect undefined terms, conflicting statements, incomplete branches, missing states, conflicting designs, and mismatches between title, description, acceptance criteria, and comments.
phases.detail: ambiguity · contradiction · stale comment · hidden assumption · unresolved decision

phases.name: Testability analysis
phases.desc: Check whether every expected behaviour has an observable result, controllable precondition, accessible environment, stable data setup, and measurable success condition.
phases.detail: observable · controllable · repeatable · measurable · isolated

phases.name: Risk and dependency mapping
phases.desc: Identify roles, permissions, tenants, devices, integrations, migrations, notifications, analytics, accessibility, performance, security, and backward-compatibility impact.
phases.detail: direct dependencies · indirect dependencies · operational risk · customer risk

phases.name: Question and recommendation drafting
phases.desc: Write concise questions that request concrete decisions. Keep assumptions separate and never silently turn them into requirements.
phases.detail: decision owner · required answer · impact if unanswered · suggested default

phases.name: Stakeholder review
phases.desc: Present the findings grouped by blocker, material gap, improvement, and optional clarification. Bind accepted decisions to the ticket revision.
phases.detail: blocking gaps · accepted assumptions · owner · due date

phases.name: Publish review record
phases.desc: Generate a ticket-ready summary, testability verdict, traceable decision log, and follow-up checklist. Reopen the review if the ticket changes materially.
phases.detail: idempotent comment · revision hash · unresolved items · change trigger

verdicts.label: READY
verdicts.desc: The ticket is sufficiently clear and testable for the agreed scope.

verdicts.label: READY WITH ASSUMPTIONS
verdicts.desc: Work may continue only with explicitly recorded, owned assumptions.

verdicts.label: NEEDS CLARIFICATION
verdicts.desc: Material questions remain but do not yet prove the ticket is invalid.

verdicts.label: BLOCKED
verdicts.desc: A missing decision, source, environment, or dependency prevents responsible implementation or testing.

verdicts.label: OUT OF SCOPE
verdicts.desc: The item is not a product-behaviour ticket or requires another review process.

evidence: Quoted text is short, contextual, and traceable to its source.
Frame/version and affected state are identified.
Schema version, status behaviour, and ownership are explicit.
Actor, ownership, and allowed operation are named.
Owner, timestamp, chosen option, and revision are recorded.
Every acceptance criterion maps to a controllable test and evidence type.
controls: The skill may suggest options but cannot choose product behaviour without an authorised decision.
Every material statement cites a ticket section, design, contract, or explicit stakeholder decision.
A material ticket or design update invalidates the prior READY verdict.
Customer names, credentials, private URLs, and attachments follow access and retention policy.
Questions request one concrete decision and explain the consequence of leaving it unanswered.
The reviewer identifies conflicts but does not impersonate Product, Engineering, Security, or Legal ownership.

decisions.label: BLOCKED
decisions.desc: A required decision, source, owner, or test mechanism is unavailable.

decisions.label: NEEDS CLARIFICATION
decisions.desc: Material ambiguity or contradiction remains.

decisions.label: READY WITH ASSUMPTIONS
decisions.desc: Explicit assumptions are approved, owned, and time-bounded.

decisions.label: READY
decisions.desc: The reviewed revision is clear, internally consistent, and testable for the agreed scope.

boundaries: Clear requirements can still describe the wrong product decision; this skill reviews quality and testability, not product-market correctness.
Historical comments may be stale. The latest authorised decision must be identified explicitly.
Designs and API contracts can diverge; the skill flags the conflict but cannot choose the source of truth.
Non-functional expectations may need specialist review and measurable service objectives.
A READY verdict applies only to the reviewed revision and linked source versions.
Small tickets may use a lightweight mode, but skipped checks must remain visible.
skills.example_request: Review ticket QA-2201 before refinement. Focus on roles, error handling, analytics, and whether the acceptance criteria are testable.
skills.example_output:
Verdict: NEEDS CLARIFICATION

Blocking questions:
1. Which roles may edit the configuration after creation?
2. What should the user see when the external service times out?
3. Is analytics expected for both successful and failed submissions?

Testability gap:
The phrase “loads quickly” has no measurable threshold or target environment.

skills.title: Risk-based test plan generation
skills.summary: Creates a reviewable test plan from approved requirements, implementation context, and known risk, with explicit scope, required scenarios, evidence, data, and exit criteria.
skills.use_when: Use after requirements are sufficiently clear and before manual or automated execution begins.
skills.not_for: Do not use to approve unclear requirements, invent expected behaviour, or claim coverage for combinations that were not selected.

phases.name: Input and revision validation
phases.desc: Resolve approved requirements, ticket revision, designs, API contracts, implementation diff when available, target environments, and supported platforms.
phases.detail: source versions · implementation status · environment · supported matrix

phases.name: Risk model construction
phases.desc: Score customer impact, change complexity, data sensitivity, permission exposure, integration risk, reversibility, observability, and historical defect concentration.
phases.detail: likelihood · impact · detectability · recoverability · confidence

phases.name: Coverage dimension discovery
phases.desc: Identify actors, roles, tenants, states, platforms, browsers, devices, locales, network conditions, data shapes, feature flags, and upgrade paths.
phases.detail: coverage dimensions · equivalence groups · mandatory combinations

phases.name: Scenario design
phases.desc: Create atomic scenarios with purpose, priority, requirement trace, preconditions, data, steps, expected result, assertion type, evidence, and cleanup.
phases.detail: positive · negative · boundary · state transition · recovery · regression

phases.name: Matrix optimisation
phases.desc: Use risk-based selection, pairwise reasoning where appropriate, and explicit equivalence assumptions to reduce combinations without hiding exclusions.
phases.detail: selected combinations · excluded combinations · equivalence rationale

phases.name: Entry, stop, and exit criteria
phases.desc: Define what must be true before testing, when execution should stop, and how scenario outcomes map to completion or release readiness.
phases.detail: entry criteria · stop conditions · exit criteria · defect thresholds

phases.name: Peer review and approval
phases.desc: Present coverage, risk, assumptions, exclusions, test-data actions, estimated effort bands, and open questions for review.
phases.detail: coverage gaps · reviewer comments · revised scope

phases.name: Freeze and publish plan
phases.desc: Create a versioned plan with stable scenario IDs. Material requirement, build, or scope changes create a new revision rather than silently changing approved tests.
phases.detail: plan hash · revision · owner · change log · downstream references

verdicts.label: APPROVED
verdicts.desc: The plan is accepted for execution against the recorded scope and revision.

verdicts.label: APPROVED WITH GAPS
verdicts.desc: Known, owned exclusions remain and are visible in the exit criteria.

verdicts.label: REVISION REQUIRED
verdicts.desc: Coverage, traceability, data, evidence, or expected results need correction.

verdicts.label: BLOCKED
verdicts.desc: Planning cannot complete because required requirements, environment, or ownership decisions are missing.

verdicts.label: SUPERSEDED
verdicts.desc: A newer approved revision replaces this plan.

evidence: Every required behaviour links to at least one scenario or a justified exclusion.
Priority is based on impact and likelihood, not test-author preference.
Included and excluded combinations are explicit.
No expected outcome is invented from implementation alone.
Evidence can directly support the intended conclusion.
Ownership, side effects, and cleanup are defined before execution.
controls: Scenario identity survives wording edits and is never reused for a different test.
Required scenarios map to approved requirements, risks, or historical defects.
Coverage percentage excludes out-of-scope dimensions rather than implying they were tested.
Material source changes invalidate or revise the plan.
Destructive or external side effects require later execution approval.
The plan author cannot silently self-approve when policy requires independent review.

decisions.label: BLOCKED
decisions.desc: Required planning inputs or decisions are missing.

decisions.label: REVISION REQUIRED
decisions.desc: The plan is incomplete, unsafe, untraceable, or inconsistent.

decisions.label: APPROVED WITH GAPS
decisions.desc: Execution may proceed with documented, accepted exclusions.

decisions.label: APPROVED
decisions.desc: The plan is traceable, risk-based, executable, and appropriately scoped.

boundaries: A test plan predicts useful coverage; it does not prove the product works.
Pairwise reduction is unsuitable when particular combinations carry unique regulatory, security, or platform risk.
Effort is expressed as bands unless reliable execution history exists.
Unknown implementation details may require a later impact-analysis revision.
Automation suitability and execution priority are related but separate decisions.
Emergency work may use a reduced plan, but the omitted dimensions and accepted risk must be explicit.
skills.example_request: Create a test plan for QA-3302. Cover Admin and Member roles, Chrome and Samsung Tizen, failed API calls, upgrade behaviour, and regression around existing playlists.
skills.example_output:
Plan status: REVISION REQUIRED

Reason:
The ticket does not define expected Member behaviour for editing an inherited playlist.

Prepared:
- 18 draft scenarios
- 6 required P0/P1 scenarios
- Chrome and Tizen coverage matrix
- Network failure and upgrade scenarios

Pending:
Product decision for inherited playlist permissions.

skills.title: Structured exploratory QA session
skills.summary: Runs a time-boxed exploratory session with a clear charter, controlled data, evidence, notes, coverage map, findings, and follow-up recommendations.
skills.use_when: Use when learning a new feature, searching for unknown risks, investigating behaviour beyond scripted cases, or evaluating usability and resilience.
skills.not_for: Do not use as unstructured clicking, as a replacement for required scripted verification, or as permission to test destructive ideas in shared environments.

phases.name: Session preflight
phases.desc: Confirm environment, build identity, role, tenant, data boundaries, allowed tools, time box, and whether customer or production data is prohibited.
phases.detail: build · environment · charter owner · time box · role · data boundary

phases.name: Charter definition
phases.desc: Write one focused mission describing the target, risks, users, and questions. Split broad missions into separate sessions.
phases.detail: explore target · with resources · to discover information

phases.name: Heuristic and tour selection
phases.desc: Choose relevant tours such as feature, data, claims, interruption, configuration, platform, accessibility, consistency, recovery, and misuse.
phases.detail: selected heuristics · reason · excluded tours

phases.name: Data and state preparation
phases.desc: Create isolated data, capture starting state, define reversible actions, and record any stubs, clocks, flags, or network shaping.
phases.detail: starting state · resource IDs · side effects · cleanup

phases.name: Exploration and note capture
phases.desc: Explore deliberately, branching from observations while recording timestamps, actions, questions, ideas, evidence references, and state transitions.
phases.detail: observations · questions · test ideas · coverage notes · interruptions

phases.name: Finding reproduction and classification
phases.desc: Attempt to reproduce interesting behaviour, distinguish defects from usability concerns and questions, and preserve the original path when reproduction fails.
phases.detail: reproduction confidence · severity hypothesis · environment dependence

phases.name: Debrief
phases.desc: Review what was covered, what remained untouched, strongest findings, unanswered questions, data created, and whether another charter is justified.
phases.detail: coverage map · findings · risks · follow-up charters

phases.name: Publish session record and clean up
phases.desc: Publish a concise session report, proposed defects, and follow-up work. Clean verified owned data and record residual state.
phases.detail: session notes · evidence bundle · defect proposals · cleanup report

verdicts.label: NO MATERIAL FINDING
verdicts.desc: The session found no material issue within its explicit charter and coverage.

verdicts.label: FINDINGS RECORDED
verdicts.desc: One or more reproducible defects, risks, usability concerns, or requirement questions were identified.

verdicts.label: FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED
verdicts.desc: Promising leads or uncovered risk justify another targeted session.

verdicts.label: BLOCKED
verdicts.desc: The session could not meaningfully explore the charter because of environment, access, or data limits.

verdicts.label: ABORTED
verdicts.desc: The session ended early and the completed coverage is preserved.

evidence: Key branches and state transitions can be reconstructed.
Relevant context, build, role, and state are visible.
Original event and later reproduction attempts are separated.
The concern describes friction, not personal preference alone.
Explored and unexplored areas are distinguished.
Created, changed, and remaining resources are identified.
controls: The session records pauses, interruptions, and actual exploration time.
Material detours become notes or new charters rather than silently replacing the mission.
Absence of a finding is never presented as comprehensive product coverage.
Destructive, privacy-sensitive, external, or production-like actions require explicit approval.
A non-reproducible observation keeps its first evidence and confidence level.
Raw notes remain available; the polished report cannot erase uncertainty or skipped areas.

decisions.label: BLOCKED
decisions.desc: The charter could not be explored meaningfully.

decisions.label: FINDINGS RECORDED
decisions.desc: Material findings require triage or action.

decisions.label: FOLLOW-UP REQUIRED
decisions.desc: The session produced useful leads but insufficient coverage or certainty.

decisions.label: NO MATERIAL FINDING
decisions.desc: No material issue was found within the stated charter and time box.

boundaries: Exploratory testing is sampling, not proof of absence.
Time boxes limit depth; uncovered areas must remain visible.
Usability observations may require user research or product validation.
Intermittent behaviour may remain unresolved after one session.
A broad feature often needs several narrow charters.
Shared environments can constrain aggressive recovery, load, or misuse exploration.
skills.example_request: Run a 60-minute exploratory session on the new offline playlist recovery flow. Focus on interrupted downloads, reboot, clock changes, and reconnect behaviour.
skills.example_output:
Session outcome: FINDINGS RECORDED

Charter:
Explore offline playlist recovery to discover data loss, stale state, and confusing recovery behaviour.

Material finding:
After reboot during a partial download, the player remains on the previous playlist but reports the new playlist as active.

Coverage:
Completed interruption, reboot, and reconnect tours.
Clock-change tour was not completed.

Follow-up:
Create a focused session for clock and certificate-expiry behaviour.

skills.title: Evidence-backed defect report
skills.summary: Converts an observed problem into a precise, reproducible, environment-bound defect report without overstating cause, severity, or scope.
skills.use_when: Use after a potential product issue has been observed and enough evidence exists to support triage.
skills.not_for: Do not use to convert every inconclusive result into a bug, assign blame, guess root cause, or expose secrets and customer data.

phases.name: Observation intake
phases.desc: Capture the original observation, reporter wording, timestamps, environment, build, role, tenant, affected object, and existing evidence without rewriting uncertainty.
phases.detail: original statement · first evidence · reporter · time · environment

phases.name: Environment and build verification
phases.desc: Confirm deployment identity, device or browser, OS, player version, configuration, flags, network, account state, and whether the issue occurred in production or a test environment.
phases.detail: artifact digest · source commits · platform · configuration · role

phases.name: Reproduction design
phases.desc: Create the shortest controlled reproduction that preserves necessary preconditions and separates setup from the failing action.
phases.detail: preconditions · minimal steps · expected result · actual result · cleanup

phases.name: Reproduction attempts
phases.desc: Attempt reproduction without retrying until success. Record every attempt, data variation, timing, and environment difference.
phases.detail: attempt outcomes · frequency · first failure retained · non-reproducible evidence

phases.name: Classification and impact
phases.desc: Classify the issue type, affected users and platforms, frequency, recoverability, data or security impact, workaround, and confidence. Keep severity separate from scenario priority.
phases.detail: category · severity · release blocking · scope · confidence

phases.name: Duplicate candidate review
phases.desc: Search existing issues by symptom, component, platform, error fingerprint, and root-cause clues. Present candidates for human decision rather than auto-closing the report.
phases.detail: candidate IDs · similarity · differences · status

phases.name: Report drafting
phases.desc: Write a concise title, verified environment, preconditions, steps, expected and actual results, frequency, impact, evidence, logs, and notes. State hypotheses as hypotheses.
phases.detail: plain language · stable links · redacted evidence · no unsupported root cause

phases.name: Review and publication
phases.desc: Review accuracy, privacy, severity, ownership, and linked evidence. Publish idempotently and preserve the local report revision.
phases.detail: approver · report hash · ticket ID · publication status

verdicts.label: CONFIRMED DEFECT
verdicts.desc: Controlled evidence demonstrates product behaviour that contradicts an approved expectation.

verdicts.label: PROBABLE DEFECT
verdicts.desc: Evidence is strong but reproduction, scope, or expectation has limited uncertainty.

verdicts.label: NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT
verdicts.desc: The behaviour is expected or belongs to environment, data, automation, or third-party failure.

verdicts.label: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE
verdicts.desc: The observation cannot yet support a responsible defect report.

verdicts.label: DUPLICATE CANDIDATE
verdicts.desc: An existing issue may represent the same problem and requires a human decision.

evidence: Screenshot, video, trace, log, or customer evidence
Source, time, platform, and privacy status are recorded.
All attempts and variations remain visible.
Requirement, design, contract, or authorised decision
Expectation is sourced rather than inferred from preference.
The evidence supports the exact claimed mismatch.
Severity rationale is separate from probability and priority.
Similarity and meaningful differences are stated.
controls: Code clues may be listed as hypotheses but never presented as confirmed cause without evidence.
Secrets and personal data are filtered before storage and publication.
Severity uses defined impact criteria; urgency and stakeholder pressure do not silently change it.
Failed, passed, aborted, and environment-error attempts are all retained.
Automated similarity cannot suppress a new issue without review.
Retries update the same draft or issue rather than creating duplicates.

decisions.label: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE
decisions.desc: The report cannot responsibly claim a product defect.

decisions.label: NOT A PRODUCT DEFECT
decisions.desc: Evidence points to expected behaviour or another failure class.

decisions.label: PROBABLE DEFECT
decisions.desc: A report may be published with explicit uncertainty and follow-up.

decisions.label: CONFIRMED DEFECT
decisions.desc: Evidence supports publication as a product defect.

boundaries: A defect may be real even when immediate reproduction fails.
Customer evidence may be incomplete or privacy-sensitive and should not be treated as controlled execution.
Severity can change as scope becomes clearer.
Similar symptoms can have different causes across platforms.
Logs may contain baseline noise and require versioned fingerprints.
Publication systems may truncate large evidence; preserve a durable local bundle.
skills.example_request: Create a defect report for the player showing Ethernet as Active after switching back to Wi-Fi. I have before and after screenshots and reproduced it twice.
skills.example_output:
Classification: CONFIRMED DEFECT

Title:
Network status remains “Ethernet” after the active connection changes to Wi-Fi

Frequency:
2 of 2 controlled attempts

Expected:
Device Information shows the interface currently used by the player.

Actual:
Content reconnects through Wi-Fi and the IP address changes, but Active remains “Ethernet”.

Evidence:
Before and after screenshots, network request log, and attempt ledger attached.

skills.title: Defect classification and prioritisation
skills.summary: Reviews an incoming issue and determines what it most likely represents, how severe it is, who should own it, what evidence is missing, and what action should happen next.
skills.use_when: Use for new defects, support escalations, failed test results, production observations, or issues returning from engineering.
skills.not_for: Do not use to close reports automatically, assign blame, replace incident command, or declare root cause without evidence.

phases.name: Issue snapshot
phases.desc: Freeze the current issue revision, comments, attachments, environment details, linked releases, and current status before interpretation.
phases.detail: issue revision · reporter · timestamps · links · current owner

phases.name: Evidence quality assessment
phases.desc: Check whether the issue contains an observable mismatch, sourced expectation, environment identity, reproduction detail, impact evidence, and privacy-safe attachments.
phases.detail: complete · partial · contradictory · stale · inaccessible

phases.name: Failure-class analysis
phases.desc: Evaluate product defect, expected behaviour, requirement gap, environment failure, test-data failure, automation failure, third-party failure, duplicate candidate, security concern, and unknown.
phases.detail: candidate classes · supporting evidence · contradicting evidence

phases.name: Scope and impact analysis
phases.desc: Estimate affected users, platforms, versions, tenants, data, permissions, recoverability, workaround, frequency, and customer visibility.
phases.detail: breadth · depth · permanence · recoverability · detectability

phases.name: Severity and release-blocking assessment
phases.desc: Apply defined severity criteria separately from priority and scenario criticality. Record uncertainty and escalation triggers.
phases.detail: severity · priority recommendation · release blocking · confidence

phases.name: Ownership and next-action mapping
phases.desc: Identify the team or role best positioned to investigate, the minimum next evidence, and whether the issue belongs in product backlog, incident flow, support follow-up, or test infrastructure.
phases.detail: owner · next action · due condition · escalation path

phases.name: Human triage review
phases.desc: Present classification, severity rationale, duplicate candidates, unknowns, and proposed disposition for confirmation.
phases.detail: accepted class · accepted severity · owner · unresolved questions

phases.name: Update issue and audit record
phases.desc: Update the existing issue idempotently, preserve the previous state, link evidence, and record who approved the change.
phases.detail: status transition · comment · labels · owner · audit event

verdicts.label: PRODUCT DEFECT
verdicts.desc: Evidence supports a product behaviour mismatch.

verdicts.label: EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR
verdicts.desc: The observed result matches the approved requirement or documented limitation.

verdicts.label: ENVIRONMENT OR DATA ISSUE
verdicts.desc: The failure originates outside the product behaviour under review.

verdicts.label: AUTOMATION ISSUE
verdicts.desc: The test implementation, fixture, selector, timing, or runner caused the result.

verdicts.label: REQUIREMENT GAP
verdicts.desc: No authorised expectation exists or sources conflict.

verdicts.label: UNKNOWN
verdicts.desc: Evidence cannot yet distinguish the leading classifications.

evidence: Status and comments can be traced to the triage time.
The claimed behaviour is visible or measurable.
The expected behaviour has an owner and revision.
Version, platform, tenant, and frequency data
Observed scope is distinguished from inferred scope.
Rationale addresses data, security, availability, workaround, and affected users.
The proposed owner has a clear investigation boundary.
controls: Expected-behaviour and duplicate recommendations require human confirmation.
A shared rubric prevents pressure or reporter seniority from changing severity silently.
The workflow may remain UNKNOWN instead of forcing a confident classification.
Potential security or privacy findings follow restricted handling and disclosure policy.
Reclassification does not erase earlier evidence or decisions.

verdicts.label: CANCELLED
verdicts.desc: The work no longer needs transfer and the reason is recorded.

evidence: Build, environment, role, data, and device are exact.
The receiver knows what must not be reset or deleted.
Questions and ownership transfer are recorded.
controls: Credentials are provided through approved access systems, never the handoff text.
A changed build, environment, or ticket invalidates or updates the handoff.
Not-tested and blocked work is as visible as completed work.
Security, customer, and incident evidence uses appropriate access.
The receiver should not need to infer where to start.
Sending a document is not the same as accepted transfer.

decisions.label: STALE
decisions.desc: Refresh the handoff because the source state changed.

decisions.label: BLOCKED
decisions.desc: Resolve access or prerequisite gaps before transfer.

decisions.label: READY WITH RISKS
decisions.desc: Transfer with explicit uncertainty and recovery guidance.

decisions.label: READY
decisions.desc: Transfer ownership with a verified continuation path.

boundaries: A handoff can become stale quickly in active releases or incidents.
Some physical device state cannot be captured fully in text.
Receiver availability and access may change after acceptance.
Long-running observations need explicit clocks and ownership.
Large evidence bundles may require separate restricted storage.
The handoff should remain short enough to use while linking deeper sources.

skills.title: Evidence-based QA retrospective
skills.summary: Reviews a completed release, incident, project, or testing cycle to identify escaped-risk patterns, process failures, effective controls, and owned preventive actions.
skills.use_when: Use after releases, incidents, major defects, automation migrations, or recurring QA pain.
skills.not_for: Do not use for blame, performance ranking, unsupported storytelling, or creating actions without owners and validation measures.

phases.name: Scope and psychological-safety preflight
phases.desc: Confirm event, time window, participants, facilitator, data sources, privacy, no-blame principle, and what decisions the retrospective may make.
phases.detail: event ID · window · participants · data boundary

phases.name: Evidence timeline
phases.desc: Build a factual sequence of requirements, code changes, test planning, execution, defects, decisions, rollout, incidents, recovery, and customer signals.
phases.detail: event · timestamp · source · fact · uncertainty

phases.name: Outcome and escape analysis
phases.desc: Identify what succeeded, what failed, escaped defects, false alarms, delayed detection, repeated manual work, missing coverage, and operational cost.
phases.detail: impact · detection point · escape path · recovery

phases.name: Contributing-system analysis
phases.desc: Examine requirements, architecture, ownership, environment, data, automation, observability, release controls, communication, and incentives without reducing the event to one person.
phases.detail: contributing condition · evidence · interaction

phases.name: Control effectiveness review
phases.desc: Assess which prevention, detection, containment, and recovery controls worked, failed, were missing, or produced false confidence.
phases.detail: control · expected · actual · gap · confidence

phases.name: Action design
phases.desc: Create specific preventive, detective, recovery, or learning actions with owner, due condition, priority, success measure, cost, and dependency.
phases.detail: action · owner · measure · due · dependency

phases.name: Review and commitment
phases.desc: Present the narrative, uncertainties, proposed actions, rejected actions, and ownership. Separate consensus from unresolved disagreement.
phases.detail: accepted · rejected · unresolved · owner

phases.name: Publish and follow-up
phases.desc: Publish the retrospective, create linked work items, schedule outcome reviews, and close actions only after the defined success measure is observed.
phases.detail: retro ID · action tickets · review date · evidence

verdicts.label: EFFECTIVE
verdicts.desc: The control or practice reduced risk as intended.

verdicts.label: PARTIALLY EFFECTIVE
verdicts.desc: The control helped but had material limits or gaps.

verdicts.label: INEFFECTIVE
verdicts.desc: The control did not prevent, detect, contain, or recover as expected.

verdicts.label: MISSING
verdicts.desc: No relevant control existed for the observed risk.

verdicts.label: FALSE CONFIDENCE
verdicts.desc: The control appeared healthy while failing to measure the real risk.

verdicts.label: NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE
verdicts.desc: The retrospective cannot support a confident conclusion.

evidence: The point where the risk could have been prevented or detected is evidenced.
Scope and recovery cost are not exaggerated.
The control's purpose and limitation are explicit.
Completion criteria measure outcome, not document creation alone.
An action closes only after effectiveness is checked.
controls: Analysis focuses on system conditions, decisions, and controls while preserving accountability for actions.
Recollections are useful but labelled and checked against records.
Prefer a small number of high-value owned actions over a long unprioritised list.
Training, documentation, or automation is not assumed effective without a measure.
Customer, security, incident, and personnel data follow the correct audience policy.
Actions have review dates and cannot disappear after publication.

decisions.label: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE
decisions.desc: Collect missing records before drawing material conclusions.

decisions.label: SYSTEMIC RISK
decisions.desc: High-impact missing or false-confidence controls require priority action.

decisions.label: IMPROVEMENT PLAN
decisions.desc: Owned actions address material but manageable weaknesses.

decisions.label: HEALTHY WITH LEARNING
decisions.desc: Controls were broadly effective and refinements are recorded.

boundaries: Retrospectives are vulnerable to hindsight bias.
Not every incident justifies a new automated test or process gate.
Actions can create cost or delay elsewhere and need trade-off review.
Some outcomes depend on external vendors or rare conditions.
A single event may not prove a general pattern.
The retrospective needs later evidence to show that actions worked.
skills.example_request: Run a QA retrospective for the release where a webOS black-screen issue escaped to customers. Focus on requirements, platform coverage, automation, rollout monitoring, and support detection.
skills.example_output:
Retrospective outcome: SYSTEMIC RISK

Key finding:
The release smoke suite treated webOS 6 as one equivalence group, although laboratory evidence already showed model-specific browser differences.

False-confidence control:
A single representative device passed and was reported as webOS 6 coverage.

Actions:
1. Split the platform matrix by browser engine and model family.
2. Add repeat-launch playback coverage.
3. Add model-segmented rollout telemetry.
4. Review effectiveness after the next two webOS releases.
